description: Actor identifiers, and the ones that MUST be refused. An identifier takes one of exactly two forms -- an address 'local@domain', or a namespaced name 'namespace/name' -- is lowercase ASCII, and is rejected rather than normalized when it is not. Provenance records are blocks, so an identifier that two implementations spell differently is two block_ids for one fact: the silent divergence canonical serialization exists to prevent, re-entering through a field nobody canonicalized. Every rejection names its reason, because a refusal a caller cannot act on is a refusal they will work around.

grammar.address: local '@' domain. local is 1..64 of [a-z0-9._%+-], does not begin or end with '.', and carries no consecutive dots. domain is 1..255, two or more labels separated by '.', each label 1..63 of [a-z0-9-] beginning and ending with [a-z0-9].
grammar.namespaced: namespace '/' name. Exactly one '/'. Each segment is 1..128 of [a-z0-9._-] and begins and ends with [a-z0-9].
grammar.common: Lowercase ASCII only, no whitespace, no control characters, at most 320 characters in total. A value carrying both '@' and '/' is ambiguous and MUST be refused.

vectors.name: address_form
vectors.note: A person by an address they already hold. The form most identifiers take, and the reason no scheme prefix is stored: this is what people already write, correctly, without being asked twice.

vectors.name: address_form_minimal
vectors.note: The shortest thing the address form accepts. Present so that an implementation tightening a length bound has something to fail against.

vectors.name: namespaced_person
vectors.note: A person known only by a handle. The protocol must not require an address here: a contributor who has one to give is not the only kind of contributor an open brain hears from.

vectors.name: namespaced_runtime
vectors.note: A runtime. The namespace carries the party that made it, which is why no separate organization member exists anywhere in a record.

vectors.name: namespaced_model
vectors.note: A model. Indistinguishable in form from a runtime on purpose: what a party is, is recorded beside the identifier, never encoded into it.

vectors.name: namespaced_with_dots_in_the_name
vectors.note: A dot inside a name segment is ordinary. Model names carry them, and a grammar that refused would push implementations into inventing a spelling.

vectors.name: namespaced_pipeline
vectors.note: A deterministic pipeline. Nothing about the form says it is software rather than a person; the kind beside it does.

vectors.name: bare_word
vectors.reason: neither an address nor a namespaced name
vectors.note: The value this rule exists to refuse. A role noun means nothing off the machine that wrote it, so two brains cannot agree that two records name the same party, and provenance records are blocks: the disagreement is silent and permanent.

vectors.name: bare_name
vectors.reason: neither an address nor a namespaced name
vectors.note: A first name is a bare word with a friendlier face. It resolves to nobody.

vectors.name: uppercase_local_part
vectors.note: Refused rather than lowered. Normalizing would mint a block_id the caller did not ask for, and an identifier the caller cannot predict is one they cannot search for either.

vectors.name: uppercase_domain
vectors.note: A domain is case-insensitive in the world and byte-sensitive here. Two spellings of one address are two block_ids for one fact.

vectors.name: uppercase_namespace
vectors.note: The same rule, on the other form. One rule, applied to the whole value, is what keeps it checkable in five lines.

vectors.name: scheme_prefix
vectors.reason: the local part carries a character the address form does not admit
vectors.note: The URI wrapper is not stored. It is ceremony around a value already written correctly, and an implementation exporting to a format that wants URIs derives one at that boundary.

vectors.name: url
vectors.note: The reason a URL is not the stored form: a trailing slash, a default port and a percent-encoded octet are three normalization questions, and a canonical form must not leave any of them open.

vectors.name: empty_namespace
vectors.note: A namespace that names nobody namespaces nothing.

vectors.name: empty_name
vectors.note: The mirror case, which a naive split on the separator accepts.

vectors.name: nested_namespace
vectors.note: Exactly one separator, so that splitting is unambiguous without a longest-match rule that two implementations could read differently.

vectors.name: empty_domain
vectors.note: An address form with nothing to resolve against.

vectors.name: empty_local_part
vectors.note: A domain is not a person.

vectors.name: single_label_domain
vectors.note: A domain with no dot is machine-local, which is the same failure as a bare word wearing an at-sign.

vectors.name: embedded_space
vectors.note: Whitespace has no canonical treatment here, and a value that must be trimmed before comparison is a value two implementations will trim differently.

vectors.name: both_forms
vectors.note: Ambiguous by construction: an implementation that decided which form wins would be deciding for every other implementation too.

vectors.name: consecutive_dots
vectors.reason: consecutive dots in the local part
vectors.note: Admitted by a permissive dot-atom reading and refused here, because the spelling has no single canonical form in the wild.

vectors.name: leading_hyphen_segment
vectors.reason: a segment does not begin with a letter or a digit
vectors.note: A leading hyphen is how an option prefix sneaks into a name, and it reads as a flag to half the tools that will ever print it.

vectors.name: empty
vectors.note: Named so that an implementation checking min-length has a vector rather than an assumption.
